jobDescription: A convenience-store chain refits around twenty stores a year while they keep trading. The project manager plans each refit with the shopfitting contractor and the store team, controls spend against the store budgets, runs the pre-handover safety walk and prepares the progress reporting for the regional property board. The next programme needs a project manager who has already led a multi-site refit programme, holding the contractor relationship and budget sign-off, because the current programme manager is moving to another region. The role reports to the head of property and works with store operations, the shopfitting contractor and the company's health-and-safety team.
requirements: Plans refit schedules with the shopfitting contractor and store managers around trading hours.
Tracks spend against store budgets and prepares variation requests.
Has led a multi-site refit programme, holding the contractor relationship and budget sign-off.
Runs pre-handover safety walks and snagging with the contractor.
Prepares monthly progress reporting for the regional property board.

evidence.text: Project coordinator, then assistant project manager, at Fernhill Foodstores from May 2021 to August 2024, working on the 2023 refit of 22 convenience stores across the south-west region.
Built the weekly refit schedule for each store with the shopfitting contractor and the store manager, putting noisy work into the overnight hours when the store was closed.
Tracked spend against each store's budget in the property team's cost tracker and drafted variation requests for the programme manager to approve.
Ran the pre-handover safety walk with the contractor's site supervisor at each store and logged snags in the handover checklist.
Compiled the monthly progress summary, covering stores completed, open snags and budget variances, which the programme manager presented to the regional property board.
Work sample: the completed handover checklist for one store, listing 31 snag items with an owner, due date and close-out date for each, signed by the contractor's site supervisor and the candidate.

Reference call notes (informal, the shopfitting contractor's former site supervisor): said the candidate 'was the one really running the refit programme', 'held the purse strings for us' and that the programme manager 'mostly left it to the candidate'.
HR verification note: employment dates at Fernhill Foodstores and the titles project coordinator and assistant project manager were confirmed in the employer's written reference.

propositions.text: The candidate built the weekly refit schedule for each store with the shopfitting contractor and the store manager.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the scheduling work directly.

propositions.text: The candidate tracked store spend in the cost tracker and drafted variation requests for the programme manager to approve.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the tracking work and places approval with the programme manager.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the 22-store refit programme and held budget sign-off for the shopfitting contractor.
propositions.rationale: The claim rests on an outside contractor's informal impressions, which are hearsay about internal authority and not a record of approvals; the resume shows the candidate drafting variations for the programme manager to approve and preparing reports that the programme manager presented.

signatures: mostly left it to the candidate

gold.expectedGap: The sources show a coordinating role on a multi-site programme with approvals held by the programme manager; budget sign-off and programme leadership are not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the scheduling, cost-tracking, safety-walk and reporting work with the programme manager's approval boundary; the contractor's remarks are impressions and do not establish who held the budget.
followUpTargets: Ask which budget or contractor decisions on the 2023 refit the candidate approved personally and what the candidate's approval limit was.
